name: Question 15
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/bd8650a856fe3136759d81a886b2d4622cf3eb463b75e6023b44083c72f63a1a.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{1}{5},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $sec⁡\theta .$
worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13931905/assets/734eef45985ddfb6450666e1dd32c6d3beab9ca3aef66c87c6ba393d6960b08b.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{1}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{1}{5}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{1}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{1}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{24}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5}.$

Knowing that $sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
sec⁡\theta =\frac{1}{(\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{5})}=\frac{5}{2\sqrt{6}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}sec⁡\theta  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{5}{2\sqrt{6}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{6}}{2\cdot 6} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{6}}{12}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 15
?

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the y-coordinate of the point P is 15, use the Pythagorean identity to find sec⁡θ.

a
62
b
5612
c
962
d
569
e
7612
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Any point (x,y) on the unit circle is related to the central angle θ as follows:

x=cos⁡θ,y=sin⁡θ

We're given that y=15 at the point P. Therefore, we have

sin⁡θ=15.

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find cos⁡θ:

sin2⁡θ+cos2⁡θ=1cos2⁡θ=1−sin2⁡θcos⁡θ=±1−sin2⁡θ

Substituting sin⁡θ=15 gives

cos⁡θ=±1−(15)2=±1−125=±2425=±265.

We select the positive answer since cos⁡θ is positive in the first quadrant. So, cos⁡θ=265.

Knowing that sec⁡θ=1cos⁡θ, we have sec⁡θ=1(265)=526.

Finally, we rationalize the denominator. sec⁡θ=526=526⋅66=562⋅6=5612
